title: 利上げ見送り、中立派・中川氏反対の衝撃　会合の空気は「次はやるぞ」
extracted_text:
日銀が利上げ見送りを決めた4月の金融政策決定会合で、反対が3票入ったことが市場や政府関係者の間で話題になっている。反対3票は黒田東彦前総裁の時代のマイナス金利政策の決定時（反対4票）以来の多さだ。それ以上に、中川順子審議委員が「反・執行部票」を投じたことの意味は重い。

「中川氏の反対票は誰しもが驚いた」――。長年日銀の決定会合を見てきた野村証券の岩下真理エグゼクティブ金利ストラテジストは3会合連続の利上げ見送りとなった4月会合についてこう振り返る。

決定会合で議決権を持つのは、執行部の正副総裁3人と審議委員6人の計9人。このうち利上げ見送りに反対票を投じたのは高田創、田村直樹、中川の3氏だ。高田、田村両氏は9人のなかでも利上げに前向きな「タカ派」とされ、見送り時に反対票を投じるケースが目立った。

利上げ見送りなどの議案は執行部がまとめる。中川氏は反対票を投じたことがないうえに、金融経済懇談会での発言から特に執行部と考えが近い「中立派」と評された。その中川氏が「反・執行部票」を出したことは市場の想定外だった。

中川氏は利上げ見送りの反対理由を「中東情勢の不透明感はあるが、経済情勢を踏まえると緩和的な金融環境の下で物価の上振れリスクが高い」とした。物価上昇に対して利上げが後手に回る「ビハインド・ザ・カーブ」懸念がうかがえる。

植田和男総裁は賛成票を投じた政策委員の間でも「物価の上振れリスクはみな気にしている」と指摘した。4月の経済・物価情勢の展望（展望リポート）では物価見通しを大幅に上方修正した。

そもそも政策委員9人のうち、利上げ見送りに賛成した小枝淳子氏や増一行氏は「高田、田村両氏に次ぐ準タカ派」（日銀幹部）と受け止める向きもある。小枝氏と増氏も加われば過半数の5人が利上げ支持になる。

執行部は9人の議論を踏まえて議案を作るだけに利上げの確度が高まる。決定会合に参加した一人は「『次はやるぞ』という空気だった」と振り返る。植田氏は表決が割れたことに関し「議長として深刻に受け止めないといけない」と述べた。

決定会合での中川氏を知る人物は「時間がたつにつれ会合で発言するようになった」と言及した。その上で「普段の発言を聞くとタカで、市場に伝わっていなかっただけ」とみる。

日銀幹部も「元々タカ派なところがあり、自分の票のインパクトが最大化するタイミングを狙ってきたのでは」と話す。一方で、政府内には「執行部が反対票を入れさせたのではないか」と勘繰る声もある。

中川氏は次回の6月会合が任期中最後となる。「ある意味で守るものがない」（市場関係者）ことが予想外の動きにつながったと見る。東短リサーチなどによると、1日時点で市場は日銀が6月会合で利上げに動く確率を6割半ばと見積もる。

7月以降、中川氏は金融引き締めに慎重な「リフレ派」とみられている青山学院大教授の佐藤綾野氏に交代する。「隠れタカ派」の中川氏がいる6月会合で利上げ見送りになれば、リフレ派の佐藤氏に代わる7月以降の利上げはさらにハードルが上がりそうだ。

（竹内宏介）
translated_text:
At the Bank of Japan's April monetary policy decision meeting where the rate hike postponement was decided, the 3 dissenting votes have become a topic among market and government observers. 3 opposing votes is the most since the negative interest rate policy decision during former Governor Kuroda's term (which had 4 opposing votes). Beyond that, the significance of Director Jun Nakagawa casting an 'anti-management vote' is profound." 'Nakagawa's opposition vote surprised everyone.' - Maruha Iwashita, Executive Interest Rate Strategist at Nomura Securities who has long observed the BoJ's policy meetings, reflected on the April meeting where rate hikes were postponed for the third consecutive time.

The Policy Decision Council has voting rights held by 9 members: 3 top executives (Governor and Deputy Governors) and 6 policy board members. Among these, the 3 who voted against the postponement were Takamasa Tsukada, Naoki Tamura, and Jun Nakagawa. Tsukada and Tamura are considered 'hawks' favorable to rate hikes among the 9 members, so their opposition votes at the time of postponement stood out.

Resolutions like rate hike postponements are prepared by the management side. Nakagawa had never cast an opposition vote before and was characterized as a 'centrist' close to management's thinking based on remarks at the Financial Economic Forum. The fact that Nakagawa cast an 'anti-management vote' was beyond market expectations.

Nakagawa's reason for opposing the rate hike postponement was: 'While there is uncertainty regarding the Middle East situation, based on the economic conditions, there is a high upside risk to prices under an easing monetary environment.' This suggests concerns about rate hikes lagging behind price increases - a 'behind the curve' scenario.

Governor Kazuo Ueda, who cast a supporting vote, also pointed out that policy board members are all concerned about upside price risks. The April Economic and Price Outlook (Outlook Report) significantly revised upward the price forecast.

Indeed, among the 9 policy board members, some view those who supported the rate hike postponement, such as Junko Oeda and Kazuyuki Masu, as 'quasi-hawks next to Tsukada and Tamura' (BoJ official). If Oeda and Masu joined, the majority of 5 would support rate hikes.

Since management prepares resolutions based on the 9 members' discussions, the likelihood of rate hikes increases. One participant in the decision council reflected: 'The atmosphere was 'we'll do it next time.'' Ueda stated regarding the split vote: 'As chair, I must take this seriously.'

A person familiar with Nakagawa at the decision council noted that 'over time, she became more vocal at meetings.' Furthermore, they observed that 'her usual remarks were hawkish, it just wasn't conveyed to the market.'

BoJ officials also commented that 'she was originally hawkish, perhaps timing her vote's impact to maximize.' On the other hand, there are voices in the government speculating whether 'management induced the opposition vote.'

Nakagawa's June meeting will be her last in her term. Market observers note that 'in a sense, having nothing to defend' may have led to this unexpected move. According to Tochu Research and others, as of June 1, the market estimates about 65% probability of the BoJ taking action at the June meeting.

From July onward, Nakagawa will be replaced by Professor Ayano Sato of Aoyama Gakuin University, viewed as a 'reflationist' cautious on monetary tightening. If rate hikes are postponed at the June meeting with the 'hidden hawk' Nakagawa gone, rate hikes from July onward with the reflationist Sato would face an even higher barrier.
title_en: Interest Rate Hold Draws Shock as Centrist Nakagawa Opposes; Meeting Mood: 'We'll Do It Next Time'
